OPTIMUS-AF


Nationwide, decentralised randomised trial (n = 520) in persistent or permanent atrial fibrillation with side effects attributed to rate-control therapy, comparing a double-blind double-dummy N-of-1 crossover of metoprolol versus verapamil against standard care. PI Morten Lamberts, Herlev and Gentofte Hospital. Funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark (2027 to 2031). Responsible for investigational medicinal product, N-of-1 methodology, and CYP2D6 and drug concentration analyses.


2027




Cardiovascular Pharmacogenetics & Biobank Linkage


Deterministic individual-level linkage across Danish nationwide health registries and the Copenhagen Hospital Biobank (CHB) evaluating clinical outcomes associated with CYP2C19 loss-of-function variants in antiplatelet therapy, SLCO1B1-mediated statin uptake, and bedside clinical decision support.


2025




SAMSON-2 Trial


Investigator-initiated, nationwide, 11-center randomized controlled trial comparing a digital double-blind N-of-1 trial platform against guideline-directed standard care titration to systematically differentiate statin-associated muscle symptoms from expectation bias. Funded by the Capital Region of Denmark, Bispebjerg Hospital, and Hørslev-Fonden. Protocol approved in CTIS (2025-524955-30-01); protocol paper submitted to American Heart Journal in October 2026.


2024




TDM-VISION


Prospective clinical research project evaluating therapeutic drug monitoring algorithms and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic exposure metrics for targeted oral therapies (ibrutinib and venetoclax) in chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Funded by the Danish Cancer Society (DKK 2.3M).


2024




SPOCK Trial & European PGx Networks


Multinational European clopidogrel pharmacogenomics consortium investigating CYP2C19 genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy, alongside active working group participation in COST Action CardioPharmGeneNet and CPIC guideline development.

I am a physician and specialty registrar in clinical pharmacology studying how pharmacogenetic test results change prescribing and patient outcomes. I combine Danish national registry data with prospective clinical trials to measure whether genotype-guided dosing reduces adverse drug reactions and treatment failures.
My current work focuses on CYP2C19-guided antiplatelet therapy, SLCO1B1 genotyping for statin intolerance, and therapeutic drug monitoring of targeted cancer therapies.
